sentences.en: As Americans, I think we're used to the idea that land can be owned.
sentences.zh: 作为美国人，我认为我们已经习惯了土地可以被拥有的观念。

sentences.en: Whether it's a beachfront or, say, a stream bed.
sentences.zh: 无论是海滨还是，比如说，一条溪流的河床。

sentences.en: And if you own the land, you can, just for example, build on it.
sentences.zh: 如果你拥有这片土地，你就可以，举个例子，在上面盖房子。

sentences.en: Or sell its water rights.
sentences.zh: 或者出售它的水权。

sentences.en: Or you can keep other people from ever accessing it.
sentences.zh: 又或者你可以禁止其他人进入。

sentences.en: We just accept it as the way that things naturally work.
sentences.zh: 我们只是把它当作事物自然运作的方式来接受。

sentences.en: Like a lot of our laws, we inherited this way of looking at land ownership from England.
sentences.zh: 就像我们的许多法律一样，我们从英国继承了这种看待土地所有权的方式。

sentences.en: When I went there, I found that a growing group of people are thinking about ownership of land and access to land very differently than Americans are.
sentences.zh: 当我到那里时，我发现越来越多的人对土地所有权和土地使用权的看法与美国人截然不同。

sentences.en: And they're thinking that, while property might belong to somebody, it doesn't mean other people shouldn't be able to walk on it or picnic or camp on it.
sentences.zh: 他们认为，虽然财产可能属于某人，但这并不意味着其他人不应该能够在上面行走、野餐或露营。

sentences.en: It's a vision of land and the outdoors that's so radically different from ours that I had to go see it for myself.
sentences.zh: 这是一种与我们截然不同的土地和户外愿景，我必须亲自去看看。

sentences.en: My name is Brooke Jarvis, and I'm a contributing writer to the New York Times magazine.
sentences.zh: 我叫布鲁克·贾维斯（Brooke Jarvis），是《纽约时报》杂志的特约撰稿人。

sentences.en: This week's Sunday Read is about a group of English activists who are pushing for more rights to explore England's natural spaces.
sentences.zh: 本周的《周日阅读》讲述了一群英国活动家，他们正在争取更多探索英国自然空间的权利。

sentences.en: One way these activists do this is through mass trespasses, which are actually a kind of protest that dates back more than a century.
sentences.zh: 这些活动家采取的一种方式是“大规模非法入侵”，这实际上是一种可以追溯到一个多世纪前的抗议形式。

sentences.en: They're pushing for something that a lot of other European countries already have.
sentences.zh: 他们正在争取许多其他欧洲国家已经拥有的东西。

sentences.en: A right to roam.
sentences.zh: 漫游权。

sentences.en: I went to England this past spring, where I joined two of these events.
sentences.zh: 去年春天我去了英国，参加了其中两场活动。

sentences.en: One was at the Kinder Reservoir in the Peak District near Manchester.
sentences.zh: 其中一场是在曼彻斯特附近的峰区（Peak District）的金德水库（Kinder Reservoir）。

sentences.en: It lies underneath a tall plateau of Moreland called Kinder Scout, which is where one of the most famous trespasses of the 1930s happened.
sentences.zh: 它位于一片名为金德侦察兵（Kinder Scout）的高原荒地之下，那是20世纪30年代最著名的非法入侵事件发生地之一。

sentences.en: The activists planned to take a dip in the water as a form of protest to show that people needed more access to open water swimming.
sentences.zh: 活动家们计划在水中游泳，以此作为一种抗议形式，表明人们需要更多进入开放水域游泳的机会。

sentences.en: I went to another trespass that was led by someone in a local folk choir in Bristol.
sentences.zh: 我参加了另一场非法入侵活动，由布里斯托尔当地一个民谣合唱团的成员领导。

sentences.en: We headed out to this very old castle that has been in the same family since shortly after the Norman Conquest and walked around the fields and grounds.
sentences.zh: 我们前往一座非常古老的城堡，自诺曼征服后不久，它就一直属于同一个家族，我们在田野和庭院里走了一圈。

sentences.en: We stopped in a little patch of woodlands along the way and sang songs together.
sentences.zh: 途中我们在一小片林地停下来，一起唱歌。

sentences.en: Many of the activists I wrote about traced the start of their involvement to the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我所写的许多活动家都将他们参与的起点追溯到疫情期间。

sentences.en: They had a real hunger to be outside, but they kept finding out that they had a lot less access to the land around them than they'd realized.
sentences.zh: 他们非常渴望到户外去，但他们不断发现，自己对周围土地的接触权远比他们意识到的要少。

sentences.en: People told me they felt trapped, walled off from the natural world.
sentences.zh: 人们告诉我，他们感到被困住了，被隔绝在自然世界之外。

sentences.en: There was all this space around them that they couldn't get into.
sentences.zh: 他们周围有那么多空间，却无法进入。

sentences.en: And they began rethinking what was possible.
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始重新思考什么是可能的。

sentences.en: So here's my article,
sentences.zh: 这是我的文章，

sentences.en: The Fight for the Right to Trespass, read by Gabra Zachman.
sentences.zh: 《争取非法入侵权的斗争》，由加布拉·扎克曼（Gabra Zachman）朗读。

sentences.en: The signs on the gate at the entrance to the path and along the edge of the reservoir were clear.
sentences.zh: 小径入口处大门上以及水库边缘的标志清晰可见。

sentences.en: No swimming, they warned.
sentences.zh: 警告写着：禁止游泳。

sentences.en: White letters on a red background.
sentences.zh: 红底白字。

sentences.en: On a chill mid-April day in northwest England, with low gray clouds and rain in the forecast, the signs hardly seemed necessary.
sentences.zh: 在英格兰西北部一个寒冷的四月中旬，天空低垂着灰云，预报有雨，这些标志似乎根本没必要。

sentences.en: But then people began arriving, by the dozens and then the hundreds.
sentences.zh: 但随后人们开始到达，先是几十人，然后是几百人。

sentences.en: Some walked only from nearby hayfield, while others came by train or bus or foot from many hours away.
sentences.zh: 有些人只是从附近的干草地走过来，而另一些人则是坐火车、乘巴士或步行了许多小时才赶到。

sentences.en: In a long trailing line, they tramped up the hill beside the dam and around the shore of the reservoir, slipping in mud and jumping over puddles.
sentences.zh: 他们排成长长的队伍，在大坝旁的山坡上跋涉，绕过水库岸边，在泥泞中滑倒，跳过水坑。

sentences.en: Above them rose a long, curving hill of open moorland, its heather still winter brown.
sentences.zh: 在他们上方，隆起了一座弯曲的开阔荒地长山，石楠花依然呈现着冬日的棕色。

sentences.en: When they came to a gap between a stone wall and a metal fence, they squeezed through it, one by one, slipping under strings of barbed wire toward the water below.
sentences.zh: 当他们来到石墙和金属栅栏之间的缝隙时，他们一个接一个地挤过去，从铁丝网下钻过，向下方水域走去。

sentences.en: On the steep, grassy bank above the reservoir, coats and sweaters came off, revealing wetsuits and swimsuits, thermoses of tea and hot chocolate were readied for quick access.
sentences.zh: 在水库上方陡峭的草坡上，人们脱下外套和毛衣，露出潜水服和泳衣，保温杯里的茶和热巧克力也准备好随时享用。

sentences.en: Someone had brought along a banged-up trumpet with which to provide the appropriate fanfare.
sentences.zh: 有人带来了一把破旧的小号，用来吹奏合适的号角声。

sentences.en: There were seasoned winter swimmers, people who had stories of breaking through ice for a dip, and complete newbies, deciding as they shivered whether this particular symbolic act
sentences.zh: 这里有经验丰富的冬泳者，他们有在冰层中凿洞游泳的故事；也有完全的新手，在寒颤中思考这种象征性的行为

sentences.en: was really for them.
sentences.zh: 是否真的适合他们。

sentences.en: There was a seven-year-old who swam in a knit beanie with a purple pom-pom and a man with a Yorkshire accent who told his wife, in mock horror,
sentences.zh: 有一个七岁的孩子戴着紫色绒球的针织帽在游泳，还有一位约克郡口音的男士假装惊恐地告诉他的妻子：

sentences.en: I had to ask a strange woman to zip me up, Mary.
sentences.zh: 玛丽，我不得不请一位陌生的女士帮我拉拉链。

sentences.en: Down on the shore, giggling and shrieking people picked their way across slippery rocks.
sentences.zh: 在岸边，人们嬉笑着、尖叫着，在湿滑的岩石上小心翼翼地行走。

sentences.en: Then, with a great deal of cheering and splashing, they took to the water en masse, fanning out in all directions.
sentences.zh: 随后，在一阵欢呼和水花声中，他们集体下水，向四面八方散开。

sentences.en: Some carried a large banner that read,
sentences.zh: 有些人举着一条大横幅，上面写着：

sentences.en: The Right to Swim.
sentences.zh: 游泳权。

sentences.en: The water was somewhere around 50 degrees Fahrenheit, but it felt, a 61-year-old swimmer announced after climbing out and wrapping up again, bloody wonderful.
sentences.zh: 水温大约在华氏50度（约10摄氏度），但一位61岁的游泳者在爬上岸重新裹好衣服后宣布，这感觉“棒极了”。

sentences.en: She handed her sister a cheddar and Branston pickle sandwich and told me she usually hates encountering crowds when they go swimming, but that this one was delightful.
sentences.zh: 她递给姐姐一个切达干酪和布兰斯顿泡菜三明治，并告诉我她通常讨厌在游泳时遇到人群，但这次感觉很愉快。

sentences.en: More rounds of cheers went up as new waves of swimmers splashed into the water.
sentences.zh: 随着一波又一波新的游泳者溅入水中，欢呼声再次响起。

sentences.en: An older woman wearing a pink floral swimsuit paused on the shore to turn to the crowd still on land.
sentences.zh: 一位穿着粉色花纹泳衣的老妇人在岸边停下，转身面对岸上的人群。

sentences.en: Don't be beaten down, she shouted, raising a fist above her flower-bedecked bathing cap.
sentences.zh: 不要被打倒，她喊道，在戴着花朵装饰的泳帽上方举起拳头。

sentences.en: Rebel!
sentences.zh: 反抗吧！

sentences.en: Then she too flopped into the lake.
sentences.zh: 然后她也跳进了湖里。

sentences.en: On the bank above the reservoir, a choir serenaded the swimmers.
sentences.zh: 在水库上方的岸边，一个合唱团为游泳者们献唱。

sentences.en: He said, all this land is my master's.
sentences.zh: 他说，这片土地都是我主人的。

sentences.en: At that, I stood shaking my head.
sentences.zh: 听到这话，我站在那里摇了摇头。

sentences.en: No man has the right to own mountains any more than the deep ocean bed.
sentences.zh: 没有人有权拥有山脉，就像没有人有权拥有深海海床一样。

sentences.en: The song, by the folk singer
sentences.zh: 这首歌由民谣歌手

sentences.en: Ewan McCall, was about another mass trespass, one that took place
sentences.zh: 尤安·麦科尔（Ewan McCall）创作，讲述了另一次大规模非法入侵事件，发生在

sentences.en: 91 years earlier above this very reservoir, during which protesters were arrested for daring to walk on hills they were told to keep off.
sentences.zh: 91年前的这个水库上方，当时抗议者因敢于在被告知禁止进入的山丘上行走而被捕。

sentences.en: Over the decades that followed, the protesters' contention that people had some inherent rights of access even to lands they did not own, which in England is most land,
sentences.zh: 在随后的几十年里，抗议者坚持认为人们对即使不是自己拥有的土地（在英国，大部分土地都是如此）也拥有某种固有的进入权，

sentences.en: because the vast majority of the country is in private hands, was enshrined in law, guaranteeing public access to this and many other parts of the countryside.
sentences.zh: 因为该国绝大多数土地都掌握在私人手中，这一主张被写入法律，保障了公众进入这里和乡村许多其他地区的权利。

sentences.en: Lately, though, the swimmers told me, those hard-won gains had begun to seem both less expansive and less secure than they once imagined.
sentences.zh: 然而，游泳者们最近告诉我，那些来之不易的成果开始显得既不那么广泛，也不那么稳固了。

sentences.en: During the pandemic, many took up open-water swimming or paddling or walking, only to be surprised at the number of places they weren't allowed to go.
sentences.zh: 疫情期间，许多人开始尝试公开水域游泳、划桨或步行，却惊讶地发现有那么多地方他们不被允许进入。

sentences.en: The reservoir, owned by a private utility company, even though it is inside the Peak District
sentences.zh: 这个水库虽然位于峰区（Peak District）

sentences.en: National Park, was one such place.
sentences.zh: 国家公园内，但由一家私营公用事业公司拥有，就是这样一个地方。

sentences.en: England's national parks are full of land that is privately owned and inhabited, farmed, mined, and hunted.
sentences.zh: 英国的国家公园里到处都是私人拥有、居住、耕种、开采和狩猎的土地。

sentences.en: The government began to push to criminalize forms of trespass never before considered to be crimes.
sentences.zh: 政府开始推动将以前从未被视为犯罪的非法入侵形式定为犯罪。

sentences.en: Then, in January, the High Court sided with a wealthy couple who wanted to keep the public from camping on an estate they bought inside
sentences.zh: 接着，在1月份，高等法院支持了一对富有的夫妇，他们想阻止公众在他们购买的庄园内露营，该庄园位于

sentences.en: Dartmoor National Park in an area called the Commons, the only place in England where wild camping, what we would call backpacking, was still considered a right.
sentences.zh: 达特穆尔国家公园（Dartmoor National Park）内一个被称为“公地”（Commons）的区域，这是英国唯一一个仍然将野外露营（我们称之为背包旅行）视为权利的地方。

sentences.en: Robert McFarlane, the English nature writer, called the ruling a nationwide wake-up call.
sentences.zh: 英国自然作家罗伯特·麦克法兰（Robert McFarlane）称这一裁决为全国性的警钟。

sentences.en: Only when the last relic of a long-lost openness was threatened did it become clear just how much was at stake.
sentences.zh: 只有当长期失落的开放性的最后遗迹受到威胁时，人们才清楚地意识到有多少东西岌岌可危。

sentences.en: Like the trespassers whose anniversary they were commemorating, the swimmers believed they were fighting for something bigger than the chance to walk up a hill or swim in a river,
sentences.zh: 就像他们纪念周年纪念日的那些非法入侵者一样，游泳者们相信他们正在为比“走上山坡或在河里游泳”更宏大的事业而战，

sentences.en: something fundamental about their relationship to the land where they lived.
sentences.zh: 那是关于他们与所居住土地之间某种根本性的关系。

sentences.en: It's not so much that we need to be granted permission, explained a woman with long gray hair and a sweatshirt that read, kayaking is not a crime.
sentences.zh: 并不是说我们需要获得许可，一位留着长灰发、穿着写有“皮划艇不是犯罪”卫衣的女士解释道。

sentences.en: It's that we need it to be recognized that we don't need permission.
sentences.zh: 而是我们需要被认可，我们根本不需要许可。

sentences.en: Centuries ago, high moors like those of Kinder Scout, the plateau that stretched above the reservoir, were considered king's land, uncultivated areas to which access was free.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪前，像金德侦察兵（Kinder Scout）那样的高地荒原——即延伸在水库上方的高原——被认为是国王的土地，是人们可以自由进入的未开垦区域。

sentences.en: In the villages below, land was often claimed by the aristocracy and gentry who collected taxes from the peasants who worked it.
sentences.zh: 在下方的村庄里，土地通常被贵族和乡绅占有，他们向耕种土地的农民征税。

sentences.en: But many villagers, called commoners, held shared rights to common land where they could graze their animals or plant crops or gather firewood.
sentences.zh: 但许多被称为“平民”（commoners）的村民，对公地拥有共享权利，他们可以在那里放牧动物、种植庄稼或收集柴火。

sentences.en: This type of land disappeared rapidly during the enclosure movement of the 18th and 19th centuries when the wealthy claimed wild and common lands.
sentences.zh: 这种土地在18和19世纪的圈地运动中迅速消失，当时富人占有了荒地和公地。

sentences.en: Lands that, as the jurist
sentences.zh: 正如法学家

sentences.en: William Blackstone put it, previously belonged generally to everybody but particularly to nobody as their own.
sentences.zh: 威廉·布莱克斯通（William Blackstone）所言，这些土地以前普遍属于所有人，但特别不属于任何人。

sentences.en: The movement leaned on the work of philosophers such as John Locke who argued that people could gain ownership of wastelands by working and improving them.
sentences.zh: 这场运动依赖于约翰·洛克（John Locke）等哲学家的著作，他们认为人们可以通过劳动和改良荒地来获得所有权。

sentences.en: But there were others who believed that separating people from the land was a gross injustice.
sentences.zh: 但也有人认为，将人们与土地隔离开来是一种巨大的不公正。

sentences.en: What crimes, wars, murders, what miseries and horrors would the human race have been spared, wrote Jean-Jacques Rousseau, by someone who, pulling up the stakes
sentences.zh: 让-雅克·卢梭（Jean-Jacques Rousseau）写道，如果有人拔掉木桩

sentences.en: or filling in the ditch, had cried out to his fellow humans, beware of listening to this imposter.
sentences.zh: 或填平沟渠，并向同胞大喊：“当心别听这个骗子的话，

sentences.en: You are lost if you forget that the fruits are everyone's and the earth's is no one's.
sentences.zh: 如果你忘记了果实属于大家，而大地不属于任何人，那你就完了。”那么人类将免受多少罪恶、战争、谋杀、苦难和恐怖啊。

sentences.en: As enclosures spread, many former users of the land were pushed out.
sentences.zh: 随着圈地运动的蔓延，许多曾经使用土地的人被赶了出去。

sentences.en: With no way to make a living, they drifted to cities.
sentences.zh: 由于无法谋生，他们流向了城市。

sentences.en: Kinder is not far from Manchester and Sheffield, two early centers of the Industrial Revolution whose residents like to escape the choking air by going on long walks
sentences.zh: 金德离曼彻斯特和谢菲尔德不远，这两个工业革命的早期中心，居民们喜欢通过长途跋涉来逃离污浊的空气，

sentences.en: in the countryside.
sentences.zh: 去乡村走走。

sentences.en: But many of the landowners who controlled the hills weren't fond of having walkers, known as ramblers, exploring properties they used for raising sheep and hunting grouse.
sentences.zh: 但许多控制山丘的土地所有者并不喜欢“漫步者”（ramblers）探索他们用于养羊和狩猎松鸡的土地。

sentences.en: They hired armies of gamekeepers who sometimes used attack dogs to kick the ramblers out.
sentences.zh: 他们雇佣了大量猎场看守人，有时甚至使用攻击性犬只将漫步者赶走。

sentences.en: Some ramblers in their city lives were involved in trade unions and other labor movements, and they began to bring the same spirit of organization and protest
sentences.zh: 一些漫步者在城市生活中参与了工会和其他劳工运动，他们开始将同样的组织和抗议精神带到

sentences.en: to their weekend walks.
sentences.zh: 他们的周末徒步中。

sentences.en: As the most shoutable line of the McCall song has it,
